_comment: Terms for the lesson mass-media-history. status: ok = established in Turkish sources I opened; chosen = my own choice among variants; check = plausible but not verified in a source I opened (needs a Turkish-language reviewer). Keys are concept ids or short slugs; they do not clash with the core glossary.

mass-media.note: KÜRE Ansiklopedi has an entry titled 'Kitle İletişim Araçları'; DergiPark articles write 'medya (kitle iletişim araçları)', i.e. the two are used for the same thing. 'kitle medyası' also occurs in Turkish but I did not verify it in a source I opened, so it is not used.

movable-type.note: Turkish DergiPark articles on printing history use 'hareketli harf' and also 'hareketli matbaa' (seen in search summaries only, not opened in full). 'hareketli dizgi' not verified, not used.

penny-press.note: I found no established Turkish term in a source I could open (a Turkish wiki mirror shows 'Penny basın', which is not a reliable source). The lesson uses the English name with a descriptive gloss and tells the reader so.

news-agency.note: Anadolu Ajansı's own archive and KÜRE Ansiklopedi use 'ajans' / 'haber ajansı'.

broadcasting.note: 'radyo yayını', 'televizyon yayını' are standard usages in TRT's own history pages. The English term keeps its seed-sowing etymology (etymonline, Wiktionary, Dictionary.com); in Turkish the word 'yayın' has no farming trace, the lesson says so and points to the verb 'yaymak'.

colophon.note: Used in the lesson with an explanation in the glossary card. Not verified in a Turkish source I opened; an alternative would be 'basım kaydı'.

halftone.note: Turkish printing terms vary ('yarı ton', 'ara ton', 'raster'); not verified in a source I opened.

inverted-pyramid.note: Standard in Turkish journalism teaching as far as I know, but not verified in a source I opened.

firman.note: TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi articles on Müteferrika Matbaası and Takvim-i Vekayi.

fatwa.en: fatwa (legal opinion of the Sheikh al-Islam)

sheikh-al-islam.note: TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi; Schwartz 2017 translates it as Grand Mufti.

printing-house.note: 'Müteferrika Matbaası' is the TDV article title.

corrector.note: The fatwa quoted by Schwartz names 'muṣaḥḥiḥ' as the required correctors; Turkish modern equivalent 'düzeltmen' is my gloss.

state-gazette.note: TDV article on Takvim-i Vekayi: 'first official newspaper of the Ottoman State'.
